The example you gave isn't really comparable. First, the con situation you describe is between two parties (and was actually a con), not a company that provided a service (that turned out to be misleadingly advertised) and many customers. Second, AT&T didn't get sued by the customers for punitive damages, but rather a fine was levied against them.

But onto the main point, which is why it doesn't make sense to compare it to their total revenue: people think "oh, AT&T got a slap on the wrist because the fine was nowhere near how much they make across all their products and services." But the point is not to punish everything AT&T does, just the specific practice.

Let's pick out some numbers to simplify. AT&T makes $100 bucks a year, total, cash in the bank. Of that, $25 comes from selling unlimited data plans. Of that, $5 comes from users who went over the arbitrary limit and got throttled. If AT&T gets fined $5 (or more) for their actions, the business impact of throttling is negative, because they made no money from doing so and possibly lost money. Even if AT&T gets fined less than what they earned from misleading customers, they now have a record of misbehavior. The possible of swift and more stern punishment on their next infraction stops them from trying it again (ideally).

My point is that comparing it to their overall revenue makes it look like an unjustly light punishment, but again the point isn't to bankrupt AT&T but to discourage certain business practices.

I think removed comments should show up on the affected user's comment history with a status of removed rather than disappearing entirely, and moderator/admin actions should have a mandatory workflow element which specifies a reason the action was taken and sends a notification via private message to the user in question with the following information:

  1. The action taken
  2. The reason why
  3. A link to the offending post(s) OR (in the event the post was deleted or the moderator actions made the post inaccessible to the user) a quote of the post(s)
  4. An infraction counter "this is infraction #3" for ease of moderator tracking

The interface presented to moderators can be a dropdown menu can contain default options like "duplicate post", or "illegal material", and subverses can present an interface to add subverse rules to the dropdown menu.

EDITs (for clarity):

Other shortcomings of the current comment deletion system:

on other platforms they show the comment in the offending user's comment history with a status of "removed", on voat they are also removed from the comment history in the account panel of the offending user.

This isn't just a question of direct user notification, but of recordkeeping.

If comments continue to simply vanish from histories like this rather than being flagged in the user's account pane as "removed", it would be possible for a malicious moderator to avoid the streisand effect because the user themselves might not even be aware their comments are "disappearing down the memory hole"
Needed Feature For Transparency: Mandatory User Notification Of Reason For Moderator Actions
